scope: Experimental track only. These are preregistered pilot designs, not project results. Common contract for every arm: use only the existing pilot/train/calibration/regression assets; never inspect or tune on final-temporal/final-OOD manifests or labels. Pair variants on the same commit, task, exact model/prompt/policy/tool versions and evidence snapshot; randomize variant/case order; blind the existing two-expert plus tie-break adjudication; treat case as the statistical sample and repeated trials as nested observations, not independent samples. Every added planner, lens, critic, retrieval summary, test-generation, retry, gate and composer call consumes the same inclusive B_run; tool seconds also stay under the frozen arm cap. Preserve failures, timeouts, abstentions and budget overruns; mark overruns non_comparable rather than deleting them. Tune thresholds on train/calibration, select versions on regression, and only a finally frozen winner may be run once on each final holdout under the existing one_run_record contract.

claims.claim: The existing project contract already supplies the fairness and leakage controls needed for these pilots: same inputs and inclusive B_run across LLM variants, calibration-time budget freezing, nested rather than inflated trials, evaluator-hidden gold, frozen regression promotion evidence, and one-run temporal/OOD final holdouts.

candidates.name: P1 — Routed core plus optional existing perspectives
candidates.current_gap: The first pass always spends analyst budget on all five perspectives; no measured evidence yet shows whether performance, concurrency and test perspectives are needed on every case. A pure single-perspective ablation is too coarse to evaluate safe dynamic selection.
candidates.mechanism: Keep structure and correctness as mandatory core. The Diagnosis Planner selects performance, concurrency and/or test using task text plus graph/CFG/test-edge features; deterministic must-run guards force performance for performance signals, concurrency for async/task/lock/shared-state signals, and test for changed behavior or missing TESTS links. Emit selected_perspectives and enumerated route_reason_codes in DiagnosisPlan. Planner failure, schema failure or uncertainty falls back to all five. Preserve all existing contributor/Finding/merge contracts.
candidates.expected_effect: Hypothesis: optional routing preserves Critical/High and per-perspective recall while reducing analyst calls, tokens and wall time; fallback prevents catastrophic omission.
candidates.ai_specificity: Uses the existing LLM planner for task-conditioned perspective selection, but constrains it with deterministic coverage guards and typed reasons rather than a prompt-only free-form choice.
candidates.minimal_change: Add selected_perspectives and route_reason_codes to DiagnosisPlan, three deterministic must-run predicates, routing trace fields, and a five-perspective fallback. No new agent type, perspective enum, merge rule or runtime tool.
candidates.extra_cost: Small planner-output and routing-evaluation cost; expected operational cost is lower if optional perspectives are skipped. Fixed per-perspective token caps are not reallocated, so savings are observable rather than hidden as deeper selected calls.
risks: Optional-perspective false negatives, especially cross-cutting performance/concurrency defects
Planner learns superficial task-text cues and misses graph-only risk
Apparent quality comes from deterministic guards rather than AI routing
Small perspective strata produce unstable estimates
candidates.evaluation: HYPOTHESIS: R2+ is non-inferior in Critical/High Recall and saves at least 20% analyst tokens/calls. COMPARISON: current P4 fixed-five first pass versus P4-R2+ on identical cases; same per-node caps and inclusive B_run, no unused-budget reallocation; retrospectively score planner-only selections separately from forced guards. METRICS: Critical/High Recall delta (primary), overall and five stratum recalls, optional-route precision/recall, accepted TP/1k tokens, calls, total tokens, p50/p95 wall time, grounding and safety. SAMPLE UNIT: pilot case, with trial nested; include all five defect strata and negative/unsafe cases. FAILURE CRITERION: one-sided Recall non-inferiority lower bound is not above -2pp, any optional stratum trigger recall <0.85, any new Critical/High regression, grounding >5%, or analyst token/call reduction <20%. DECISION CHANGED: pass advances routed first pass to frozen regression and makes fixed-five the deterministic fallback; failure keeps fixed-five and confines routing to optional D2 expansion.

candidates.name: P2 — Contract-bound generated diagnostic lens
candidates.current_gap: The fixed five checklists may miss framework- or domain-specific failure modes, but a new free-form perspective would violate current enums, lineage and merge contracts and could merely buy another generic retry.
candidates.mechanism: Permit at most one ephemeral generated checklist after M1 only when the planner emits an evidence_gap or unclassified root-cause reason. The lens must declare one existing owner perspective, allowed evidence types, falsification question and stop condition; it may revise/challenge that owner's contributors but cannot introduce a sixth perspective, new schema, new tool, or persistent role. Reject the lens before execution if contract fields are invalid.
candidates.expected_effect: Hypothesis: a task-conditioned checklist finds rare, blind-adjudicated true findings more efficiently than spending the same tokens on a generic second pass of the selected existing perspective.
candidates.ai_specificity: The LLM synthesizes a case-specific diagnostic lens from task, graph and unresolved evidence, while typed rails constrain its capability and output.
candidates.minimal_change: Add optional generated_checklist fields to the existing expansion request and validate ownership/evidence/stop contracts; reuse D2 lineage revision and tombstones. No role pool, training loop or new perspective enum.
candidates.extra_cost: One bounded generation plus one affected-perspective D2 pass; both replace, rather than add to, the matched replay tokens inside B_run.
risks: Prompt novelty masquerades as capability
Duplicate or ungrounded findings
Lens selection overfits evaluator taxonomy-tail cases
Contract/schema drift and harder reproducibility
No recent direct evidence in code diagnosis
candidates.evaluation: HYPOTHESIS: generated lens yields more unique accepted TP per 1k incremental tokens than a budget-matched generic D2 replay. COMPARISON: no expansion, matched replay of the highest-priority existing perspective, and one contract-bound generated lens; use evaluator-selected taxonomy-tail plus ordinary/negative development cases with labels hidden from the agent. METRICS: incremental unique gold TP, accepted TP/1k tokens, precision, duplicate rate, unsupported-finding rate, valid revision/retraction rate and contract violations. SAMPLE UNIT: case, with findings nested and trial nested. FAILURE CRITERION: no unique accepted TP, lens is not better than matched replay on TP/1k tokens, Recall lower bound is not above -2pp, grounding >5%, or any perspective/lineage/output-protocol violation. DECISION CHANGED: pass allows one ephemeral lens as optional D2; failure holds or excludes generated lenses and retains the five typed checklists.

candidates.name: P3 — Independent challenge-only verifier/critic
candidates.current_gap: The Evidence Gate checks evidence/state contracts, but may not falsify causal reasoning or severity well; conversely an added critic may duplicate merger/gate work and reduce recall by over-rejecting.
candidates.mechanism: Run one fresh-context critic after M2 and before runtime routing. It receives canonical findings, contributor slices and cited evidence, not prior chain-of-thought. Output is typed CritiqueDisposition(finding_id, contributor_id, uphold|challenge|request_runtime, reason_code, evidence_ids). It cannot create findings or mark runtime_confirmed. Evidence Gate remains final authority; challenged findings are retained in history.
candidates.expected_effect: Hypothesis: independent falsification lowers unsupported and wrong-severity findings more than a same-token self-review, without removing gold Critical/High findings.
candidates.ai_specificity: Uses a separately prompted/model-context LLM as an adversarial verifier of causal and severity claims rather than another vote or prose composer.
candidates.minimal_change: One challenge node and disposition schema referencing existing IDs; reuse Evidence Gate, lineage history, runtime eligibility and report states. No new confirmation state.
candidates.extra_cost: One bounded LLM call per case inside B_run plus blind adjudication of challenge validity; compare against an equal-token merger self-review.
risks: Correlated model errors create false assurance
Over-retraction reduces recall
Redundant with merger/Evidence Gate
Critic smuggles new unsupported claims
Extra latency consumes budget otherwise available to analysis
candidates.evaluation: HYPOTHESIS: independent critic reduces unsupported/wrong-severity findings beyond both base and budget-matched self-review with no material recall loss. COMPARISON: P4 base, P4 plus same-merger self-review, P4 plus fresh-context challenge-only critic; identical total B_run by reserving the same token slice in all augmented arms. METRICS: unsupported-finding rate, Precision, Critical/High and overall Recall, valid FP retraction rate, TP false-retraction rate, severity correction accuracy, accepted TP/1k tokens and latency. SAMPLE UNIT: case; finding adjudication is nested and confidence intervals cluster by case/repository. FAILURE CRITERION: any new Critical/High regression attributable to a critic rejection, overall Recall decline >2pp, grounding remains >5% or does not improve versus matched self-review, or critic emits a new finding/confirmation. DECISION CHANGED: pass adds a bounded challenge node; failure keeps the present merger plus Evidence Gate and removes the redundant critic.

candidates.name: P4 — Bounded ancestry-safe history retrieval
candidates.current_gap: Current exact/BM25/vector anchors and Code Graph describe the frozen source snapshot but omit why prior changes were made; raw history can also be stale, noisy or leak a later solution.
candidates.mechanism: At the frozen base commit only, deterministically retrieve at most three ancestor commits touching seed files/symbols, returning commit SHA/date, touched paths and bounded message/diff-hunk excerpts. Exclude descendants/post-cutoff history, generated artifacts and solution commits; label every row historical, never runtime evidence. Replace equal tokens from the lowest-ranked current context so the context/B_run cap is unchanged. Start without embeddings, distillation, database or persistent memory.
candidates.expected_effect: Hypothesis: bounded provenance-rich history improves evidence retrieval and diagnosis on evaluator-labeled history-relevant cases while abstaining on history-irrelevant/no-gold cases, without stale-evidence false positives.
candidates.ai_specificity: Retrieval is deterministic and auditable; the LLM's AI role is to decide whether ancestral rationale supports or contradicts a diagnosis, under the same evidence gate.
candidates.minimal_change: Add a HistoryEvidence row and a base-commit ancestry filter to the existing context manifest; reuse lexical anchors, token pruning, evidence IDs and source hashes.
candidates.extra_cost: Local git traversal/indexing and a small fixed context slice; no new service or embedding model. Additional provenance adjudication is required.
risks: Stale rationale conflicts with current code
Later-fix leakage if ancestry boundary is wrong
Commit messages are incomplete or misleading
History tokens displace more useful source context
Retrieval hit improvements may not improve final findings
candidates.evaluation: HYPOTHESIS: history increases evidence Recall@10 and accepted TP/1k tokens on history-relevant cases without harming irrelevant/no-gold cases. COMPARISON: current retrieval versus current plus equal-budget bounded history; stratify evaluator-hidden history-relevant and history-irrelevant/no-gold cases. METRICS: file/function Accuracy@K, evidence Recall@5/10, gold evidence/1k tokens, downstream Critical/High Recall and Precision, history-attributed unique TP, abstention, stale/misleading-history findings, retrieval latency. SAMPLE UNIT: case; retrieval queries and findings are nested. FAILURE CRITERION: non-positive delta in both evidence Recall@10 and accepted TP/1k on the relevant stratum, any history-caused Critical/High FP or post-cutoff access, overall Recall lower bound not above -2pp, or cost p95 worsens with no quality gain. DECISION CHANGED: pass advances bounded history as an optional context source; failure keeps snapshot retrieval and excludes a history memory layer.

candidates.name: P5 — Ephemeral focused test generation
candidates.current_gap: The current focused-test path can run authorized existing commands, but an eligible High/Critical hypothesis may have no discriminating existing test. Treating an unvalidated generated test as evidence would be unsafe and circular.
candidates.mechanism: Only after a statically supported, runtime-eligible correctness/concurrency finding lacks a target existing test, generate one ephemeral test in a read-only-source overlay. The generator cannot edit production source, existing tests, manifests or evaluator files. The ExecutionPolicy exact-matches the overlay command. Evaluator-only validation later checks that the test fails on the frozen buggy commit and passes on the known fixed commit, is hermetic across repeated clean runs, and did not access hidden artifacts. Only validated executions become RuntimeEvidence; invalid tests remain failed/inconclusive artifacts.
candidates.expected_effect: Hypothesis: generated tests increase RuntimeConfirmationCoverage and useful rejection of false hypotheses on eligible findings where existing focused tests are absent, without unsafe execution or flaky evidence.
candidates.ai_specificity: An LLM converts a bounded finding plus source/CFG evidence into an executable counterexample; deterministic policy, isolation, repeated execution and evaluator-hidden differential validation decide whether it counts.
candidates.minimal_change: Add an ephemeral generated_test request kind, overlay path and validation status to the existing command manifest/RuntimeEvidence envelope; reuse eligibility, opt-in, timeout, hashes and lifecycle states.
candidates.extra_cost: One bounded generation call plus isolated test runs and evaluator-only buggy/fixed differential validation; likely the highest wall-time pilot, so restrict to eligible findings lacking existing tests.
risks: Test encodes the finding prose rather than intended behavior
False oracle or implementation-specific assertion
Flakiness, file/network/time side effects
Hidden-test or fixed-patch leakage
Generated test consumes budget without confirming/rejecting a finding
candidates.evaluation: HYPOTHESIS: generated tests add at least 5pp RuntimeConfirmationCoverage on the evaluator-owned eligible cohort and at least 80% of attempted tests pass differential/hermetic validation. COMPARISON: current P4 existing-focused-test path versus P4 plus generated test only after existing-test absence/inconclusive state; same cases, B_run and ExecutionPolicy caps. METRICS: RuntimeConfirmationCoverage (primary), completed-attempt coverage, true-hypothesis confirmation, false-hypothesis rejection, differential validity (buggy fail/fixed pass), three-clean-run stability, unsafe/policy violations, cost per confirmed TP and C/H Recall. SAMPLE UNIT: case, with evaluator-owned eligible finding nested; trials are nested. FAILURE CRITERION: <80% valid attempted tests, <5pp confirmation-coverage gain, any source/evaluator mutation or hidden-artifact access, any unsafe execution, any unstable validated test, new Critical/High regression, or overall Recall decline >2pp. DECISION CHANGED: pass advances ephemeral diagnostic test generation behind policy; failure retains existing-test execution only and excludes generated tests from evidence.

candidates.name: P6 — Calibrated uncertainty-driven execution shadow policy
candidates.current_gap: The deterministic runtime router is safe but may under/over-trigger; the design deliberately removed free-form confidence, and hosted models may not expose hidden states needed by recent latent estimators.
candidates.mechanism: Build a shadow logistic or GBDT ranker only from observable typed artifacts already produced before execution: unresolved_path/evidence_gap, contributor disagreement, missing TESTS edge, severity/evidence class, runtime eligibility, static-signal count and prior tool outcome cluster. Do not use self-reported confidence or chain-of-thought. Train on paired evaluator-owned beneficial/neutral/harmful labels, calibrate by repository-disjoint folds, and allocate the same number of calls/tool seconds as the deterministic router. Keep immutable ExecutionPolicy as a hard gate.
candidates.expected_effect: Hypothesis: calibrated artifact uncertainty ranks beneficial test/profile executions ahead of neutral/harmful ones under the same call budget, improving utility per call without safety loss.
candidates.ai_specificity: A learned uncertainty/utility policy combines structured agent disagreement and evidence gaps; it is more than a prompt but remains auditable and shadow-only until promoted.
candidates.minimal_change: Add a versioned pre-execution feature vector, calibrated score and shadow decision to the routing artifact; no change to executor, opt-in, policy or Finding states until promotion.
candidates.extra_cost: Offline feature/label construction, calibration and monitoring; runtime scoring is negligible and the call budget is unchanged. Sufficient paired labels are the main cost.
risks: Small labels and repository leakage overfit the ranker
Artifact disagreement may correlate with difficulty but not tool utility
Model/version drift invalidates calibration
Self-generated features create feedback loops
Unsafe calls if learned score bypasses deterministic policy
candidates.evaluation: HYPOTHESIS: uncertainty ranker improves paired utility per call versus the deterministic router at the same call/tool-second cap. COMPARISON: never, always, current deterministic, LLM self-decision, calibrated artifact ranker and retrospective oracle; use existing paired no-tool/tool outputs and label versioning. METRICS: beneficial coverage, harmful/neutral run rate, invocation Precision/Recall/F-beta/PR-AUC, utility gain per call, ECE, Brier, reliability, p95 tool time, confirmed TP/cost and unsafe runs. SAMPLE UNIT: case; paired arm/trial/finding observations are nested, with repository-disjoint calibration and regression. FAILURE CRITERION: no improvement in utility per call over deterministic routing, beneficial coverage declines >2pp, harmful-run rate increases, ECE/Brier do not beat a base-rate predictor, any unsafe call/policy bypass, or cost p95 worsens. DECISION CHANGED: pass promotes only to frozen shadow/regression comparison before operational use; failure keeps the deterministic router and does not use model self-confidence.

contradictions: Roles with Rails reports benefits from adaptive role evolution, but evaluates automatically scored structured-reasoning benchmarks and explicitly notes text-only/hand-designed-seed limitations; it cannot establish benefit for generated Python diagnostic lenses.

CommitDistill reports strong tiny-budget history retrieval hit rate, yet its downstream paired LLM evaluation finds no statistically detectable headline lift; retrieval success and diagnosis success must remain separate endpoints.

c-CRAB demonstrates that validated generated tests can operationalize review intent, while The Verification Horizon shows tests are still proxy verifiers vulnerable to instruction-test misalignment and shortcut exploitation; tests should layer under, not replace, provenance and trajectory checks.

To Call reports latent need estimators outperform model self-reports in its settings, but utility estimation remains difficult and its tools are search/calculation; this conflicts with treating raw LLM confidence as a ready profiler/test router.
unknowns: Whether the 60-case pilot contains enough evaluator-owned optional-perspective need labels and Critical/High events for the -2pp non-inferiority gate; power remains to be calculated after pilot variance is observed.
Which structure/correctness core and deterministic must-run triggers maximize optional-route safety for framework DI, reflection and async edge cases.
Whether an independent critic adds signal beyond the current merger, planned opposing review and Evidence Gate when total B_run is held fixed.

Whether history-relevant and natural no-history cases can be labeled with reliable provenance without exposing future fixes, and whether commit prose contains enough signal in the selected Python repositories.
How many runtime-eligible findings lack a usable existing focused test, and what fraction of generated tests can satisfy buggy-fail/fixed-pass plus hermeticity without seeing the fixed patch.
Whether hosted model APIs expose stable token probabilities/hidden states; if not, whether observable artifact features have adequate calibration and transport across model/prompt versions.
The final trial count, multiplicity correction and sample sizes for temporal and OOD endpoints; these must be set by pilot power analysis, not by the current target of three trials.
recommended_followups: Preregister the six arm definitions, exact variant hashes, common B_run/tool-second caps, case-level analysis, thresholds, randomization and blind adjudication before running any development case.

Run P1 first because it establishes the lower-cost routed baseline used by every later comparison; record planner-only decisions separately from deterministic forced perspectives so AI routing contribution is identifiable.

In parallel on disjoint development artifacts, curate evaluator-owned history-relevant/no-history labels for P4 and runtime-eligible existing-test-absent findings for P5; keep all gold and fixed-patch artifacts inaccessible to agents.
Run P3 against both base and budget-matched self-review; do not interpret a critic win over base alone as evidence of independent verification value.

Keep P2 and P6 out of operational design until P2 beats a matched existing-perspective replay and P6 has enough paired labels for repository-disjoint calibration; neither should be justified by raw self-confidence or role novelty.

Promote only candidates that pass their pilot failure gates to frozen regression artifacts under the existing promotion gate; retain every failure/timeout/non_comparable trace and FeedbackEvent provenance.

After regression selection, freeze model/prompt/policy/router/lens/history/test/critic versions and B_run hash; execute each final-temporal and final-OOD manifest exactly once and report them separately before any pooled analysis.
